The Glenn-HT code is based on the TRAF3D code, an efficient computer code designed for simulations of flows in turbine cascades.
The code employs the full compressible Navier-Stokes equations and uses a multi-stage Runge-Kutta scheme to march in pseudo time.
The code utilizes multi-grid and implicit residual smoothing to accelerate convergence to steady state.
The k-ω turbulence model used in the code does not require the computation of the dimensionless wall distance y+, which is advantageous for complicated geometries.
The formulation for the rotating reference frame introduces additional source terms in the governing equations, but allows the grid system for the rotating geometry to be stationary.
The boundary conditions at the inlet specify the relative total temperature, relative total pressure, and inlet angle profiles, while at the exit the pressure is specified.
At walls, the normal pressure gradient is set to zero, and either the temperature or heat flux is specified, along with boundary conditions for the turbulence quantities k and ω.
The Method of Weakest Descent (MWD) is used for automatic block merging, reducing the initial number of blocks by 50-90% while maintaining grid quality.
The MWD chooses which internal face to remove to minimize the number of disqualified faces, thus diminishing the set of available faces at the slowest rate.
The MWD is able to produce results near the expected minimum number of blocks, and repeated application increases the likelihood of realizing the actual minimum.

The Glenn-HT code has been applied to study flow and heat transfer in rectangular ducts with 180-degree turns, straight channels with ribs and bleed holes, and rotating channels with ribs and 180-degree turns.
The code uses local time stepping, implicit residual smoothing, and multigrid methods to accelerate convergence to the steady-state solution.
The discretization in the Glenn-HT code is formally second-order accurate, and artificial dissipation is added to prevent odd-even decoupling.
The code can handle grids with non-contiguous grid lines across branch cuts, in addition to contiguous multi-block grid systems.
The low-Reynolds number k-ω turbulence model used in the code can model flows involving separation and adverse pressure gradients.
